lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD hammer at Gowans Hobart (AUD, no conversion, premium extra). Four close mixed early-Tasmanian or old-photo lots sold $80 to $135 in Oct 2025 to Jun 2026. Category guides range $15 to $520 (the $520 was a 70-plus Hobart studio album, not comparable). No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. Web search budget was used up, so no Armitage, Colville or national results were checked.
lots.working: Close SOLD entries (Gowans hammer, all within 24 months): $80, $110, $120, $135. The $80 lot was generic (not Tasmanian), so the lowest close Tasmanian-views sale is $110, but to stay conservative given none is the same item I use the $80 generic lot as the floor: keep = 80 / 1.22 = 65.57, round down to $65. (Using $110 would give 90.) Flip: likely resale about $110 hammer at Gowans or Armitage; less about 15% vendor commission and lotting fees ($17) and $0 postage (local auction) = about $93; 93 / 2.44 = 38.1, round down to $35. Buyer's premium 22% incl GST: $65 hammer = $79.30 all-in.
lots.confidence_reason: Captions on the views could not be read and the photographer is unidentified; all SOLD comps are close mixed lots, not the same item, and two of the four had blank descriptions. Comps are consistent though ($80 to $135).
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All nine Gowans records re-opened by lot id and title, price, bid count and listing date match the researcher. Researcher URLs replaced with lot-level API URLs. Added 397065 (Box incl Tasmanian photos, Beattie etc, $135). Downgraded nothing; 416402 noted as a small souvenir album (photos checked) so weaker than the researcher implied.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged the views: one is a power station building at the foot of a penstock running straight up a forested hill, consistent with Lake Margaret power station near Queenstown; another shows a town on a bare scarred hillside typical of Queenstown/Gormanston; several have printed captions along the lower margin (unreadable at 800px). Portraits are standard cabinet cards with studio mounts, one WW1 soldier and a regimental group. Some foxing and silvering on the large prints, corner wear.
lots.condition: Fair to good for age: foxing, some silvering and edge wear on large prints, cabinet card mounts rubbed. No obvious tears seen but most prints are overlapping in the photos.
lots.question_for_armitage: How many large landscape prints are there, and what do the printed captions and photographer names say (e.g. Lake Margaret, Queenstown, Spurling, Beattie, Winter)? Any tears, water damage or trimmed margins?
